name: @thetis/canvases
description: Canvases: boards of HTML artboards and notes on a pan-and-zoom surface, made and revised by the agent with tools and by the person in a tab of the web gateway.

tools.name: canvas_create
tools.description: Create an empty canvas: a board the person opens from Canvases in the sidebar, holding HTML artboards you add with canvas_write_board. Precondition: a title; a project id (p_…) that exists, "none" for a global canvas, or nothing for this conversation's project. Returns the canvas id, which the other canvas tools take. Artboard rules are in the `canvases` skill; read it before writing HTML.

title.description: The canvas's name, as the sidebar shows it.

project.description: A project id like p_1a2b3c4d, or "none" for a global canvas. Omitted: the project of this conversation, if it has one.

launch.description: What the person sees first: { view: "canvas" } (default) or { view: "focused", file: "Main.html" }.

pages.description: Optional pages that group artboards: [{ id, name }], ids of letters, digits, _ and -.

tools.name: canvas_list
tools.description: List the person's canvases, one line each with the id, title, artboard count, project and last change. Optionally only one project's (a p_… id) or only the global ones ("none").

project.description: A project id, or "none" for global canvases. Omitted: every canvas.

tools.name: canvas_read
tools.description: Read one canvas: its index (title, pages, every artboard's frame and props, notes, order) as JSON, then a line per artboard with its size, declared props and any problems. With sources: true, the HTML of the artboards too (all, or the ones named in boards), up to 200 KB. Use it before changing a canvas the person may have edited: they move, resize, rename and tweak artboards themselves, and a layout you rewrite blindly undoes that.

canvas.description: The canvas id (c_…), or its exact title when unique.

boards.description: With sources: only these artboard files.

tools.name: canvas_write_board
tools.description: Create or replace one artboard: a self-contained HTML page (its own <style>, no network but Google Fonts, pictures by relative path assets/<name> after canvas_asset) whose root element is sized to the frame. A new artboard gets w/h 1440×900 unless given and is placed to the right of the others unless x/y are given; an existing one keeps its frame and props unless you give them. Precondition: at most 512 KB of HTML; a file name of letters, digits, _ . - ending in .html. Returns what was written and any warnings. Artboard rules are in the `canvases` skill; read it before writing HTML.

canvas.description: The canvas id (c_…), or its exact title when unique.

file.description: The artboard's file name, like Main.html or Detail.html.

w.description: The frame's width in px (16..16384). Default 1440.

h.description: The frame's height in px. Default 900.

title.description: The name the frame shows; the file name otherwise.

page.description: The page this artboard is on (a page id); none: on every page.

expand.description: fill: the frame grows to the document's height (a scrolling page).

radius.description: Corner radius of the frame in px (a phone: 40).

props.description: Values for the props the artboard declares in its #canvas-props block, overriding their defaults.

tools.name: canvas_layout
tools.description: Change a canvas's layout without touching any HTML: the title, the launch view, the pages, artboards' frames (x, y, w, h, title, page, expand, radius, props: a key set to null drops the override), the stacking order (files named go to the front, in that order), and the notes (a sticky note or a title over a row of artboards; an id set to null deletes it, an unknown id with x, y and text creates it). Precondition: every artboard named exists. Returns what was applied and the new revision.

canvas.description: The canvas id (c_…), or its exact title when unique.

pages.description: The whole list of pages, replacing the old one.

boards.description: By file name: { x?, y?, w?, h?, title?, page?, expand?, radius?, props? }; null for title, page, expand or radius removes it.

order.description: Artboard files, back to front; the ones named move to the front in this order.

notes.description: By note id: { x, y, text, kind?: "title1", w?, maxW?, size?, bold?, color?, fill?, page? }, or null to delete. A title1 note is one bold line above a row of artboards; a note without kind is a sticky.

tools.name: canvas_asset
tools.description: Store a picture, font, stylesheet or script for a canvas's artboards, from a file in your space (path) or from base64 bytes. Precondition: a name of letters, digits, _ . - with one of the extensions png jpg jpeg gif webp svg css js json woff woff2 ttf otf mp4 webm mp3; at most 16 MB; exactly one of path or base64. Returns the relative reference to use in an artboard, like assets/hero.png.

canvas.description: The canvas id (c_…), or its exact title when unique.

name.description: The file name under assets/, like hero.png.

path.description: A file in your space to copy.

tools.name: canvas_delete
tools.description: Delete one artboard (its file and its frame; the notes stay) with board, or the whole canvas without it: every artboard, asset and note, gone for good. Returns what was deleted.

canvas.description: The canvas id (c_…), or its exact title when unique.

board.description: An artboard file name; omitted, the whole canvas is deleted.

commands.label: Read one canvas, its layout and its artboards' facts
Apply a layout patch: frames, notes, pages, props, the title
Delete a canvas or one artboard
Put a canvas in a project, or make it global
Upload one asset into a canvas
Serve an artboard and its assets to the sandboxed frame
Follow the canvases as they change
